and hence by Cauchy-Schwarz

∫|t′|≤12​logB′​X|𝒟[f~](12+it′,χ)|dt′≪k,εX1/2logOk,ε​(1)+B′/2X.\int_{|t^{\prime}|\leq\frac{1}{2}\log^{B^{\prime}}X}\left|{\mathcal{D}}[\tilde{f}]\left(\frac{1}{2}+it^{\prime},\chi\right)\right|\ dt^{\prime}\ll_{k,\varepsilon}X^{1/2}\log^{O_{k,\varepsilon}(1)+B^{\prime}/2}X.

We conclude that

𝒟⁡[f~]​(12+i​t,χ)≪∫12​logB′​X≤|t′|≤2​X5/6−εk,ε⁡|𝒟⁡[f′]​(12+i​t′,χ)|​d​t′1+|t−t′|+1+X1/2​logOk,ε​(1)+B′/2​X|t|{\mathcal{D}}[\tilde{f}]\left(\frac{1}{2}+it,\chi\right)\ll_{k,\varepsilon}\int_{\frac{1}{2}\log^{B^{\prime}}X\leq|t^{\prime}|\leq 2X^{5/6-\varepsilon}}\left|{\mathcal{D}}[f^{\prime}]\left(\frac{1}{2}+it^{\prime},\chi\right)\right|\frac{dt^{\prime}}{1+|t-t^{\prime}|}+1+\frac{X^{1/2}\log^{O_{k,\varepsilon}(1)+B^{\prime}/2}X}{|t|}

for logB′⁡X≤|t|≤X5/6−ε\log^{B^{\prime}}X\leq|t|\leq X^{5/6-\varepsilon}; by Cauchy-Schwarz, one thus has

|𝒟⁡[f~]​(12+i​t,χ)|2≪∫12​logB′​X≤|t′|≤2​X5/6−εk,ε⁡|𝒟⁡[f′]​(12+i​t′,χ)|2​d​t′1+|t−t′|​log​X+1+X​logOk,ε​(1)+B′​X|t|2.\left|{\mathcal{D}}[\tilde{f}]\left(\frac{1}{2}+it,\chi\right)\right|^{2}\ll_{k,\varepsilon}\int_{\frac{1}{2}\log^{B^{\prime}}X\leq|t^{\prime}|\leq 2X^{5/6-\varepsilon}}\left|{\mathcal{D}}[f^{\prime}]\left(\frac{1}{2}+it^{\prime},\chi\right)\right|^{2}\frac{dt^{\prime}}{1+|t-t^{\prime}|}\log X+1+\frac{X\log^{O_{k,\varepsilon}(1)+B^{\prime}}X}{|t|^{2}}.

Integrating in tt, we can bound the left-hand side of (121) for f~\tilde{f} by

≪∫12​logB′​X≤|t|≤2​X5/6−εk,ε⁡|𝒟⁡[f′]​(12+i​t,χ)|2​𝑑t​log2​X+X​logOk,ε​(1)−B′​X,\ll_{k,\varepsilon}\int_{\frac{1}{2}\log^{B^{\prime}}X\leq|t|\leq 2X^{5/6-\varepsilon}}\left|{\mathcal{D}}[f^{\prime}]\left(\frac{1}{2}+it,\chi\right)\right|^{2}\ dt\log^{2}X+X\log^{O_{k,\varepsilon}(1)-B^{\prime}}X,

so (by taking B′B^{\prime} large enough) it suffices to establish the bounds

(122) ∫12​logB′​X≤|t|≤2​X5/6−ε|𝒟[f′](12+it,χ)|2dt≪k,ε,A,B,B′Xlog−AX\int_{\frac{1}{2}\log^{B^{\prime}}X\leq|t|\leq 2X^{5/6-\varepsilon}}\left|{\mathcal{D}}[f^{\prime}]\left(\frac{1}{2}+it,\chi\right)\right|^{2}\ dt\ll_{k,\varepsilon,A,B,B^{\prime}}X\log^{-A}X

in the Type d1d_{1}, Type d2d_{2}, and Type II cases.

We first treat the Type d2d_{2} case. By dyadic decomposition it suffices to show that

∫T/2≤|t|≤T|𝒟[f′](12+it,χ)|2dt≪k,ε,A,B,B′d2(q1)Ok​(1)XlogOk,ε,B​(1)−2​AX\int_{T/2\leq|t|\leq T}\left|{\mathcal{D}}[f^{\prime}]\left(\frac{1}{2}+it,\chi\right)\right|^{2}\ dt\ll_{k,\varepsilon,A,B,B^{\prime}}d_{2}(q_{1})^{O_{k}(1)}X\log^{O_{k,\varepsilon,B}(1)-2A}X

for all logB′⁡X≤T≪X5/6−ε\log^{B^{\prime}}X\leq T\ll X^{5/6-\varepsilon}. From Corollary 2.12 we have

The Type d1d_{1} case can be treated similarly to the Type d2d_{2} case (with the role of β2​(n)\beta_{2}(n) now played by the Kronecker delta function δn=1\delta_{n=1}). It thus remains to handle the Type II case. Here we factor

𝒟⁡[f′]​(12+i​t,χ)=𝒟⁡[α]​(12+i​t,χ)​𝒟​[β]​(12+i​t,χ).{\mathcal{D}}[f^{\prime}]\left(\frac{1}{2}+it,\chi\right)={\mathcal{D}}[\alpha]\left(\frac{1}{2}+it,\chi\right){\mathcal{D}}[\beta]\left(\frac{1}{2}+it,\chi\right).

and hence

𝒟⁡[f′]​(12+i​t,χ)2=𝒟⁡[β]​(12+i​t,χ)​𝒟​[β]​(12+i​t,χ)​𝒟​[α∗α]​(12+i​t,χ).{\mathcal{D}}[f^{\prime}]\left(\frac{1}{2}+it,\chi\right)^{2}={\mathcal{D}}[\beta]\left(\frac{1}{2}+it,\chi\right){\mathcal{D}}[\beta]\left(\frac{1}{2}+it,\chi\right){\mathcal{D}}[\alpha\ast\alpha]\left(\frac{1}{2}+it,\chi\right).

At this point it is convenient to invoke an estimate of Harman (which in turn is largely a consequence of Huxley’s large values estimate and standard mean value theorems for Dirichlet polynomials), translated into the notation of this paper:

Lemma A.1.

Let X≥2X\geq 2 and ε>0\varepsilon>0, and let M,N,R≥1M,N,R\geq 1 be such that M=X2​α1M=X^{2\alpha_{1}}, N=X2​α2N=X^{2\alpha_{2}}, and M​N​R≍XMNR\asymp X for some α1,α2>0\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2}>0 obeying the bounds

|α1−α2|<16+ε|\alpha_{1}-\alpha_{2}|<\frac{1}{6}+\varepsilon

and

α1+α2>23−ε.\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2}>\frac{2}{3}-\varepsilon.

Let a,b,c:ℕ→ℂa,b,c\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{C} be Ok,ε​(1)O_{k,\varepsilon}(1)-divisor-bounded arithmetic functions supported on [M/2,2​M][M/2,2M], [N/2,2​N][N/2,2N], [R/2,2​R][R/2,2R] respectively obeying the bounds

a(n),b(n),c(n)≪k,εd2(n)Ok,ε​(1)logOk,ε​(1)Xa(n),b(n),c(n)\ll_{k,\varepsilon}d_{2}(n)^{O_{k,\varepsilon}(1)}\log^{O_{k,\varepsilon}(1)}X

for all nn. Suppose also that cc has good cancellation. Then we have

∫logB⁡X≤|t|≤X56−ε|𝒟[a](12+it)𝒟[b](12+it)𝒟[c](12+it)|dt≪k,ε,A,BXlog−AX\int_{\log^{B}X\leq|t|\leq X^{\frac{5}{6}-\varepsilon}}\left|{\mathcal{D}}[a]\left(\frac{1}{2}+it\right){\mathcal{D}}[b]\left(\frac{1}{2}+it\right){\mathcal{D}}[c]\left(\frac{1}{2}+it\right)\right|\ dt\ll_{k,\varepsilon,A,B}X\log^{-A}X

whenever A>0A>0 and BB is sufficiently large depending on AA.

Proof.

Apply [25, Lemma 7.3] with x≔X2x\coloneqq X^{2} and θ≔712+ε2\theta\coloneqq\frac{7}{12}+\frac{\varepsilon}{2} (so that the quantity γ⁡(θ)\gamma(\theta) defined in [25, Lemma 7.3] is at least as large as 13+2​ε\frac{1}{3}+2\varepsilon). Strictly speaking, the hypotheses in [25, Lemma 7.3] restricted |t||t| to be at least exp⁡(log1/3⁡X)\exp(\log^{1/3}X) rather than logB⁡X\log^{B}X, but one can check that the argument is easily modified to adapt to this new lower bound on |t||t|. ∎

If we apply this lemma with a≔β​χa\coloneqq\beta\chi, b≔β​χb\coloneqq\beta\chi, c≔(α∗α)​χc\coloneqq(\alpha\ast\alpha)\chi (with α1=α2≥13−ε20+o⁡(1)\alpha_{1}=\alpha_{2}\geq\frac{1}{3}-\frac{\varepsilon}{20}+o(1)) using Lemma 2.6 to preserve the good cancellation property, we conclude that

∫logB′⁡X≤|t|≤X56−ε|𝒟[f′](12+it)|2dt≪k,ε,A,BXlog−AX\int_{\log^{B^{\prime}}X\leq|t|\leq X^{\frac{5}{6}-\varepsilon}}\left|{\mathcal{D}}[f^{\prime}]\left(\frac{1}{2}+it\right)\right|^{2}\ dt\ll_{k,\varepsilon,A,B}X\log^{-A}X

giving (122) in the Type II case.
